These composite systems can incorporate materials such as graphene86,87 and nanoscale fillers88 to improve flexibility and alter gas diffusion mechanisms (Figure 5) to reach WVTRs in the range of 10-5 g/m2/day while maintaining high optical transparencies.89–91 Notably, the reduction in WVTRs for multilayer inorganic/polymer-composite structures demonstrates a strong dependence on the number of dyads, and WVTRs did not change significantly depending on the thickness of the inorganic layer. Note that these systems (Figure 5) do not operate as encapsulating electrodes due to their insulating design. As described next, we sought to assimilate the three areas of thin-film encapsulation that were previously introduced, spanning the state-of-the-art inorganic/organic multilayer structure, TCGDBs, and polymer composite systems to form a novel inorganic/polymer-composite encapsulating electrode. Figure 5: Concept images of emerging polymer-composite barrier systems, including (a) polymer/graphene/polymer, (b) polymer/clay nanocomposite, and (c) nanoparticle composite with an Al O organic/inorganic multilayer structure. 2 3 8/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard In this project, a transparent and conductive composite (TCC: Figure 6a and b) is introduced as a simple solution to assimilate the inorganic/polymer multilayered structure without losing electrical access through the material stack. The TCC comprises highly conductive silver-coated polymethyl methacrylate (Ag-PMMA) microsphere fillers protruding from a transparent non-conductive epoxy matrix.58–63 When employed between two TCO thin films, the dispersed monolayer arrangement of the spherical fillers facilitates an anisotropic electrical connection between the inorganic films. In effect, the in-plane conductivity of the TCO and the out-of-plane conductivity of the TCC work collectively to form a single encapsulating electrode (Figure 6c). The proposed inorganic/polymer-composite TCGDB is the first of its kind and aims to gain the benefits of incorporating polymers alongside inorganic thin-films (i.e., inorganic/polymer multilayer) to suppress diffusion pathways and to increase the operational stabilities of PSCs.21–23 As part of the project objectives, we evaluate standalone TCC specimens for their optical and electrical properties as well as permeabilities, as-synthesized, and after 1,000 hours of either outdoor exposure or damp heat in dark (85˚C, 85% R.H.) aging. These standalone TCC specimens demonstrate high optical transparencies (%T approx. 85% in the 370nm-1200nm region for 5% Ag-PMMA concentration), excellent out-of-plane electrical conductivities (R<0.2 Ω·cm²), and reasonable equilibrium permeabilities (permeability < 1 g·mm/m2/day), all of which remained virtually unchanged after aging.
